fields.acceptance: internal/api ship tests show a repo whose ship-change names a head build renders with it and one that names none renders in-process, with isRhizaRepo gone from ship; TestShipRebaseBuildsMergedHead and its related tests show ship rebase merges origin/main, then runs SHIP_HEAD_BUILD, then renders, and that a failed build pushes nothing and resets the branch; the ship-land-branch-build testscript shows ship land landing and rendering with the SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA build and failing, with nothing landed or pushed, when that build is missing; Rhiza's workflows, bugfix included, set SHIP_HEAD_BUILD and pass rhiza workflow check.
fields.statement: Ship no longer checks whether the repo is Rhiza's own. A workflow names a build of the PR head in its [env]: SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA, the binary ship's render and land run with, and SHIP_HEAD_BUILD, the shell command that builds it. Rhiza's own workflows (ship-change, docs and bugfix, which includes ship-change) set both, and their head-build steps run SHIP_HEAD_BUILD before rebase, land and rebase-merge, failing when it is empty. Ship rebase changes the head it renders, so it runs SHIP_HEAD_BUILD itself (sh -c, in the worktree) after merging origin/main and before rendering, both when settling a rendered-only conflict and before its final render; a failed build pushes nothing and resets the branch. A named binary that is missing fails ship before it lands, renders or pushes anything. A workflow that names no head build renders and lands in-process.
